title: Draft in-console copy blocks for marketplace onboarding (tooltips, instructions, error states)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
Draft copy blocks for the Console “Marketplace onboarding” wizard and supporting UI states (tooltips, inline help, button labels, and error messages). Copy must align with AWS/GCP marketplace listing copy + messaging framework, and be accurate per Security/Compliance guidance (avoid over-claiming).

Target surfaces (Console)
1) Marketplace onboarding entry point
- Banner/CTA shown to newly signed-in users who arrived from marketplace or who select “Buy via Marketplace” in pricing.
- Dedicated entry under Billing/Plans: “Cloud Marketplace subscription”.

2) Onboarding wizard steps
- Step A: Select cloud marketplace (AWS or GCP)
- Step B: Link subscription to a Redwood organization
- Step C: Select region / deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private where applicable)
- Step D: Confirm entitlements + finish

3) Entitlement status panels
- Pending sync
- Active
- Partial (base SKU active, add-on pending)
- Error / needs support

4) Error / edge-case states
- Entitlement not found (delay)
- Invalid purchase identifiers / subscription not recognized
- Subscription already linked to another org
- Org has conflicting plan (direct contract) / needs Sales assistance
- Region mismatch
- Multiple subscriptions found
- GCP project/account mismatch

Tone + constraints
- Developer-first, action-oriented, minimal jargon.
- Don’t promise certifications or controls not explicitly approved. Use “supports” / “available” language and link to Security FAQ.
- Keep customer-facing text consistent across AWS and GCP; only diverge when the workflow truly differs.
- Avoid implying that Redwood can access the buyer’s cloud account beyond receiving marketplace entitlement events.

Copy blocks (V1)

A) Entry point
1. CTA card title
- “Activate your Marketplace subscription”

2. CTA card body
- “Connect your AWS or Google Cloud Marketplace purchase to a Redwood organization to start using your plan and any add-ons.”

3. Primary button
- “Activate subscription”

4. Secondary link
- “Learn how Marketplace billing works” (links to docs FAQ)


B) Step A: Choose marketplace
Header
- “Where did you purchase Redwood?”

Options
- “AWS Marketplace”
- “Google Cloud Marketplace”

Helper text
- “We’ll use your marketplace entitlement to enable the right plan, regions, and add-ons in Redwood.”

Button
- “Continue”


C) Step B: Link to a Redwood organization
Header
- “Link subscription to an organization”

Body
- “Your Marketplace subscription must be linked to exactly one Redwood organization. If you’re joining an existing org, ask an admin to complete this step.”

Org picker label
- “Organization”

Org picker placeholder
- “Select an organization”

Tooltip (Organization)
- “The organization that will own this subscription, including usage, users, and billing settings.”

If user has no orgs
- Empty state title: “Create an organization to continue”
- Empty state body: “Marketplace purchases need an organization to attach entitlements and usage.”
- Button: “Create organization”

Checkbox (optional, if supported by flow)
- Label: “I’m an admin of this organization”
- Error (if not admin): “Only organization admins can link a Marketplace subscription.”

Button
- “Link subscription”


D) Step C: Provide purchase details / verify subscription
Note: keep as automatic as possible; only request identifiers when entitlement lookup fails.

Default (automatic)
- Title: “Verify your purchase”
- Body: “We’re checking for your Marketplace entitlement. This can take a few minutes after purchase.”

Status pill copy
- “Waiting for entitlement”

Actions
- Primary: “Refresh status”
- Secondary: “I need help”

Help drawer text
- “If you just completed purchase, wait 1–5 minutes and refresh. If it’s been longer than 15 minutes, contact support and include your Marketplace subscription ID.”

Manual entry fallback (AWS)
- Section title: “Enter AWS subscription details”
- Field label: “AWS Marketplace subscription ID”
- Placeholder: “e.g., sub-1234abcd…”
- Helper text: “Find this in AWS Marketplace → Manage subscriptions.”

Tooltip (AWS subscription ID)
- “Used only to locate your marketplace entitlement and link it to this org.”

Manual entry fallback (GCP)
- Section title: “Enter Google Cloud purchase details”
- Field label 1: “Billing account ID (optional)”
- Placeholder: “e.g., 01A1B1-2C3D4E-5F6G7H”
- Field label 2: “GCP project ID (recommended)”
- Placeholder: “e.g., my-prod-project”
- Helper text: “We use this to help match entitlements when multiple projects or accounts exist.”

Button
- “Validate and continue”


E) Step D: Confirm activation
Success title
- “Subscription active”

Success body
- “Your Marketplace plan is now active for this organization. You can start using Redwood immediately. Usage will be billed through your cloud marketplace.”

Secondary body (add-ons)
- “If you purchased add-ons (e.g., retention or premium SLA), they may take a few minutes to appear.”

Buttons
- Primary: “Go to API keys”
- Secondary: “View plan details”
- Tertiary: “Read Marketplace FAQs”


F) Plan details panel microcopy
Plan label
- “Marketplace plan”

Line items
- “Base plan”
- “Add-ons”

Add-on examples (strings only; shown when present)
- “Audit log retention (add-on)”
- “Compliance support package (add-on)”
- “Premium SLA (add-on)”

Disclaimer line
- “Plan availability and features depend on your Marketplace purchase and region.”


Error states (customer-facing)

1) Entitlement not found (likely delay)
Title
- “We haven’t received your entitlement yet”
Body
- “Marketplace entitlements can take a few minutes to sync after purchase. Wait a moment, then refresh.”
Actions
- Primary: “Refresh status”
- Secondary: “Contact support”
Support hint (small text)
- “Include your Marketplace subscription ID and the organization name.”

2) Invalid identifiers
Title
- “Subscription not recognized”
Body
- “We couldn’t match this subscription to a Redwood Marketplace product. Double-check the ID, or contact support for help.”
Action
- “Try a different ID”

3) Subscription already linked to another org
Title
- “Subscription already linked”
Body
- “This Marketplace subscription is already linked to a different Redwood organization. For security, we can’t move it automatically.”
Actions
- Primary: “Contact support”
- Secondary: “Back to organizations”
Support hint
- “If you recently changed orgs, include both org names and your subscription ID.”

4) User is not an org admin
Title
- “Admin access required”
Body
- “Only organization admins can link a Marketplace subscription. Ask an admin to complete activation.”
Action
- “Copy instructions” (copies a short message the user can paste to their admin)

Copy-to-clipboard message (for admins)
- “Please sign in to Redwood Console → Billing → Cloud Marketplace subscription → Activate subscription, and link it to the correct organization.”

5) Region mismatch
Title
- “Region doesn’t match your purchase”
Body
- “Your Marketplace plan is associated with a different region than the one selected. Switch regions, or contact support if you need help.”
Actions
- Primary: “Change region”
- Secondary: “Contact support”

6) Multiple subscriptions found
Title
- “Choose a subscription”
Body
- “We found multiple Marketplace subscriptions for your account. Select the one you want to link to this organization.”
Label
- “Subscription”

7) Conflict with direct contract / existing plan
Title
- “Plan change needs review”
Body
- “This organization already has a non-Marketplace billing plan. To avoid billing conflicts, we need to review this change.”
Actions
- Primary: “Contact Sales/Support”
- Secondary: “Cancel”


Security/compliance language blocks (approved-safe phrasing)
These are optional “Learn more” or tooltip copy blocks, not headline claims.

1) “What data does Redwood receive from the marketplace?”
- “Cloud marketplaces send Redwood entitlement events so we can activate your plan. Redwood does not need access to your cloud account to provide the service.”

2) “How is my data protected?”
- “Redwood supports encryption in transit and at rest. For details on logging, retention options, and shared responsibility, see the Marketplace Security FAQ.”

3) “Audit logs and retention”
- “Audit logging and retention options depend on your plan and any add-ons you purchased.”


Acceptance criteria
- Copy is provided for: step headers, helper text, primary/secondary button labels, tooltips, and all listed error states.
- Copy does not conflict with Marketplace listing copy or the Messaging Framework (no forbidden phrases / compliance over-claims).
- Copy has explicit guidance for entitlement delays (sets expectation + provides support path).
- Copy includes org admin requirement and “already linked” safety messaging.
- Final copy is reviewed by PMM (Soojin Lee) and Security Eng (Marcus Lin) for accuracy.

Open questions (to resolve in review)
- Do we want the “Copy instructions” action for non-admins, or keep the UI simpler with just a message?
- Should the wizard explicitly mention “Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private” at activation time, or keep it generic and let entitlements drive available options?
- For GCP: is “project ID” the only stable identifier we should request in fallback mode, or also “billing account”? (Need Eng confirmation based on entitlement ingestion behavior.)

Handoff notes for Engineering
- Error messages assume we can differentiate: pending vs not-found vs already-linked vs permission denied vs region mismatch.
- If the backend only returns a generic “not found”, we should still show the “We haven’t received your entitlement yet” message for the first 15 minutes after a purchase timestamp (if available), otherwise show “Subscription not recognized.”

Requested reviewers
- Soojin Lee (PMM) for voice/alignment with listing copy
- Marcus Lin (SecEng) for security wording
- Chloe Martin (Console backend) for feasibility of error differentiation
- Ethan Park (Entitlements mapping) for GCP/AWS identifier guidance
comments: 2025-01-24 — Kira Thompson: Drafted V0 wizard copy based on design spec. Main gaps: needs final terminology for AWS ‘subscription ID’ vs ‘agreement ID’ (waiting on Eng).

2025-01-28 — Soojin Lee: Prefer “Activate subscription” vs “Connect marketplace” for consistency with listing CTA. Also remove “compliance package” from default examples unless we confirm SKU naming matches packaging doc.

2025-01-29 — Marcus Lin: Security language is mostly OK. Please avoid “Redwood does not need access” absolute phrasing; suggest “Redwood does not require permissions into your cloud account to activate entitlements” and link to FAQ. Also ensure we don’t imply audit logs are always included—tie to plan/add-on.

2025-02-03 — Chloe Martin: We can distinguish already-linked and not-admin. Region mismatch depends on entitlement payload; likely yes for AWS, TBD for GCP. For “pending vs not-found” we can use ingestion timestamps on our side once webhook received, but we can’t read purchase time from UI reliably.

2025-02-06 — Kira Thompson: Incorporated PMM + SecEng edits. Updated security block to avoid absolutes; changed add-on examples to generic ‘retention’/‘premium SLA’ wording. Marking In Review pending confirmation from Ethan on GCP fallback fields.
